hints: Focus on how unsaturated limonene is by comparing its formula $\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{16}$ with a fully saturated alkane.
A saturated $\text{C}_{10}$ alkane would be $\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{22}$, so you are 6 hydrogens short, which means 3 units of unsaturation in total.
Subtract the one ring to leave the number of $\text{C=C}$ bonds, then remember each $\text{C=C}$ needs one $\text{H}_2$ and one mole of gas is $24\text{ dm}^3$ at room conditions.
walkthrough:
**Find the total unsaturation**

Think of how many hydrogens are missing compared to a saturated alkane. That tells you the total of rings plus pi bonds.

For $\text{C}_n\text{H}_m$, saturated acyclic is $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+2}$:
$$\text{For C}_{10}: \text{saturated} = \text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{22}$$
$$\text{Missing H} = 22 - 16 = 6$$
Each unit of unsaturation removes 2 H, so total units = $6/2 = 3$.

**Separate rings from double bonds**

You are told there is one 6-membered ring and it is the only ring. So the rest of the unsaturation must be $\text{C=C}$ bonds.

$$\text{Number of C=C} = \text{total unsaturation} - \text{rings} = 3 - 1 = 2$$

**Convert double bonds to hydrogen volume**

Each $\text{C=C}$ adds one molecule of $\text{H}_2$ in hydrogenation:
$$\text{C=C} + \text{H}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH-CH}$$
So 1 mol of limonene with 2 double bonds needs 2 mol of $\text{H}_2$. At room conditions, molar volume = $24\text{ dm}^3\text{ mol}^{-1}$:
$$V = 2 \times 24 = 48\text{ dm}^3$$

options.A: 12 dm3 is only 0.5 mol of H2. This would be correct for half a double bond per molecule, which makes no chemical sense. It often comes from dividing by 2 instead of multiplying.
options.B: 24 dm3 is 1 mol of H2, so this assumes only one C=C bond. That happens if you forget to subtract the ring, or miscount the hydrogen deficiency as only 1 double bond.
options.C: 48 dm3 is correct. C10H16 is 3 units unsaturated, minus 1 ring leaves 2 C=C bonds. 2 mol H2 per mole of limonene gives 2 x 24 = 48 dm3 at room conditions.
options.D: 72 dm3 is 3 mol of H2. This counts all 3 units of unsaturation as C=C bonds and forgets that one unit is the ring, which does not react with hydrogen.
